---
title: "Running marimo notebooks on your own computer"
---

If you are having trouble logging in to molab or opening the notebooks there,
you can run the class notebooks on your own computer instead.
These instructions work on Windows, macOS, and Linux.

You will use a free tool called
[pixi](https://pixi.prefix.dev/latest/)
that installs Python, marimo, and everything else the notebooks need,
exactly as I have them set up on my computer.
You only need to type a few short commands.

The setup has three parts, and ***you only need to do them once***:

1.  [Install pixi](#install-pixi)
2.  [Download the class files](#download-the-class-files)
3.  [Start marimo](#start-marimo)

After that, [getting back into your notebooks](#each-time-you-work-on-a-notebook)
takes two commands.

::: {.callout-note}
## Before you start

-   You will need an internet connection and about 1 GB of free disk space.
-   The first time you start marimo, it will take a few minutes to download and
    install everything. After that, it starts in a few seconds.
-   Below, choose the tab for your computer's operating system (Windows,
    macOS, or Linux). Picking a tab once will switch all the tabs on this page.
:::

## Install pixi

::: {.panel-tabset group="os"}

### Windows

1.  Download the pixi installer by clicking this link:
    [pixi installer for Windows](https://github.com/prefix-dev/pixi/releases/latest/download/pixi-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.msi)

2.  Open your Downloads folder and double-click the file you just downloaded
    (`pixi-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.msi`).
    Follow the prompts to install pixi, accepting the default options.

    If Windows shows a blue "Windows protected your PC" window, click
    "More info" and then "Run anyway."

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## The installer didn't work. Is there another way?

Yes. Open the **Terminal** app (see [Open a terminal](#open-a-terminal)
below), copy the command below, paste it into the terminal, and press Enter:

```powershell
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -c "irm -useb https://pixi.sh/install.ps1 | iex"
```
:::

### macOS

1.  Open the **Terminal** app.
    The easiest way to find it is to press **Command (⌘) + Space**,
    type `Terminal`, and press Enter.

2.  Copy the command below, paste it into the Terminal window
    (**Command (⌘) + V**), and press Enter:

    ```bash
    curl -fsSL https://pixi.sh/install.sh | sh
    ```

    You will see some messages about pixi being downloaded and installed.
    When the command is done, you will get a new prompt.

### Linux

1.  Open a terminal.

2.  Copy the command below, paste it into the terminal, and press Enter:

    ```bash
    curl -fsSL https://pixi.sh/install.sh | sh
    ```

    If you get a message that `curl` is not found, use this instead:

    ```bash
    wget -qO- https://pixi.sh/install.sh | sh
    ```

:::

::: {.callout-important}
## Close your terminal and open a new one

After installing pixi, ***close any terminal windows you have open***.
Your terminal only learns about newly installed programs when it starts, so
pixi will not work in a terminal that was already open.
:::

### Check that pixi is installed

Open a new terminal (see [Open a terminal](#open-a-terminal) below if you
are not sure how), type the following command, and press Enter:

```bash
pixi --version
```

You should see something like `pixi 0.81.0` (your version number may be
different).
If you see an error that `pixi` is "not recognized" or "command not found,"
close the terminal, open a new one, and try again.
If you still get the error, see [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting).

## Download the class files

1.  Go to the
    [class GitHub repository](https://github.com/phyletica/intro-to-comp-bio).

2.  Click the green **"Code"** button, and then click **"Download ZIP"**
    at the bottom of the menu that pops up.
    This will download a file named `intro-to-comp-bio-main.zip`.

3.  Unzip the file:

    ::: {.panel-tabset group="os"}

    #### Windows

    Open your Downloads folder, ***right-click*** `intro-to-comp-bio-main.zip`,
    choose **"Extract All..."**, and then click **"Extract."**

    Do ***not*** just double-click the ZIP file and work from inside it.
    That only lets you peek at the files; it does not unzip them.

    #### macOS

    Open your Downloads folder and double-click `intro-to-comp-bio-main.zip`.
    A folder named `intro-to-comp-bio-main` will appear next to it.

    #### Linux

    Use your file manager to extract `intro-to-comp-bio-main.zip`, or run
    `unzip intro-to-comp-bio-main.zip` from your Downloads folder.

    :::

4.  Open the unzipped folder until you see a folder named `notebooks`
    and a file named `pixi.toml`.
    On Windows, you may need to open a second `intro-to-comp-bio-main` folder
    inside the first one to find them, and `pixi.toml` may show up as just
    `pixi`.
    ***The folder that holds `notebooks` and `pixi.toml` is your class folder.***

5.  Rename your class folder to `comp-bio`, and move it into your
    ***home folder***:

    ::: {.panel-tabset group="os"}

    #### Windows

    Your home folder is the folder with your username, such as
    `C:\Users\YourName`.
    To open it, open File Explorer, click in the address bar at the top,
    type `%USERPROFILE%`, and press Enter.
    Then drag your `comp-bio` folder into it.

    #### macOS

    Your home folder is the folder with your username (it has a house icon).
    To open it, click on the desktop or a Finder window, and then in the
    Finder menu at the top of the screen choose **Go → Home**.
    Then drag your `comp-bio` folder into it.

    #### Linux

    Move the folder to your home directory (`~/comp-bio`).

    :::

::: {.callout-warning}
## Don't put your class folder in OneDrive or iCloud

On many computers, the Desktop and Documents folders are automatically
backed up to OneDrive (Windows) or iCloud (macOS).
pixi creates thousands of small files, and backing those up can make
everything very slow or cause errors.
Your home folder avoids this problem.
:::

## Start marimo

### Open a terminal

::: {.panel-tabset group="os"}

#### Windows

Click the Start button, type `Terminal`, and open the **Terminal** app.
On Windows 10, if **Terminal** doesn't show up, type `PowerShell` and open
**Windows PowerShell** instead.

#### macOS

Press **Command (⌘) + Space**, type `Terminal`, and press Enter.

#### Linux

Open your terminal app of choice.

:::

### Move into your class folder

A new terminal starts in your home folder, which is where you put your class
folder.
Type the following command and press Enter:

```bash
cd comp-bio
```

The `cd` command means "change directory" (a directory is another name for a
folder).

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## I put my class folder somewhere else. How do I get there?

Type `cd` followed by a ***space*** (don't press Enter yet).
Then drag your class folder from File Explorer or Finder and drop it onto the
terminal window.
The folder's location will be typed in for you.
Now press Enter.
:::

### Run marimo

Type the following command and press Enter:

```bash
pixi run start
```

The ***first time*** you do this, pixi will download and install Python,
marimo, and the other packages the notebooks need.
This can take several minutes, and you will see a lot of messages scroll by.
That is normal.

When it is done, marimo will open in your web browser, showing a list of the
class notebooks.
Click on a notebook to open it.
If your browser doesn't open by itself, look in the terminal for a line
starting with `http://localhost:2718` (the numbers may be different),
and copy and paste that whole address into your web browser.

::: {.callout-important}
## Keep the terminal open while you work

The terminal is running marimo for you.
If you close the terminal window, your notebook will stop working.
You can minimize the terminal, but don't close it until you are done.
:::

### When you are done

1.  Save your notebook by pressing **Ctrl + S** (Windows and Linux) or
    **Command (⌘) + S** (macOS).
    marimo also saves automatically, but it doesn't hurt to make sure.
2.  Close the browser tab.
3.  Go back to the terminal and press **Ctrl + C** to stop marimo
    (this is **Ctrl + C** on macOS too, not ⌘ + C).
    If marimo asks whether you want to shut down, type `y` and press Enter.
4.  Now you can close the terminal.

Your notebooks are saved in the `notebooks` folder inside your class folder.

## Each time you work on a notebook

Once everything is set up, here is all you need to do:

1.  [Open a terminal](#open-a-terminal).
2.  Type `cd comp-bio` and press Enter.
3.  Type `pixi run start` and press Enter.

## Getting new notebooks

When I post a new notebook during the semester, you only need to download
that one file.
Please do ***not*** download the whole ZIP file again, because your new class
folder would not contain the work you have already done.

1.  Go to the
    [notebooks folder on GitHub](https://github.com/phyletica/intro-to-comp-bio/tree/main/notebooks)
    and click into the folder for the new notebook.
2.  Click on the notebook file (it ends in `.py`).
3.  Near the top right of the file, click the **download** button
    (the icon with a downward-pointing arrow, labeled "Download raw file").
4.  Find the downloaded file in your Downloads folder, and move it into the
    `notebooks` folder inside your class folder.

The next time you run `pixi run start`, the new notebook will show up in
marimo's list of notebooks.

## Troubleshooting

### "pixi is not recognized" or "pixi: command not found"

Your terminal doesn't know about pixi yet.
Close ***all*** of your terminal windows, open a new one, and try again.
If that doesn't work, restart your computer and try again.
If you still get the error, try installing pixi again.

### "could not find pixi.toml" or "could not find a pixi workspace"

The terminal is not in your class folder.
Type the command below and press Enter to list what is in the folder your
terminal is in:

```bash
ls
```

You should see `notebooks` and `pixi.toml` in the list.
If you don't, you are in the wrong folder.
See the tip under [Move into your class folder](#move-into-your-class-folder)
for an easy way to get to the right one.
If you see another `intro-to-comp-bio-main` folder, your class folder is
inside it, so go back to step 4 under
[Download the class files](#download-the-class-files).

### "cd: no such file or directory" or "Cannot find path"

Your class folder isn't named `comp-bio`, or it isn't in your home folder.
Go back to step 5 under
[Download the class files](#download-the-class-files), or use the
drag-and-drop tip under
[Move into your class folder](#move-into-your-class-folder).

### `pixi run start` takes a very long time or fails partway through

The first run downloads a lot of files, so make sure you have a good internet
connection (campus Wi-Fi is usually fine).
If it fails partway through, run `pixi run start` again; pixi will pick up
where it left off.
If it is extremely slow, make sure your class folder is not inside OneDrive
or iCloud (see the warning under
[Download the class files](#download-the-class-files)).

### A notebook says it "Failed to download file"

Some notebooks download small data files from GitHub the first time they run.
Check that your computer is connected to the internet, and then re-run the
notebook.

### Still stuck?

Please come to office hours or send me a message.
It helps a lot if you include a screenshot of your terminal window showing
the error message.
